sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: System design problem walkthroughs — full end-to-end designs for the cases interviewers actually ask: URL shortener, distributed cache, rate limiter, news feed, ride-sharing dispatch, payment system, notification service, real-time chat. Each case follows the same structure: requirements, capacity estimation, API design, data model, high-level architecture, deep dives into the bottleneck components, and the trade-offs you would articulate to the interviewer. Pair this with the System Design Fundamentals page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Each case has a **canonical bottleneck** — find it fast, deep-dive there.

- **URL shortener** — write throughput + key-gen.
- **News feed** — fan-out-on-write vs fan-out-on-read.
- **Rate limiter** — token bucket vs leaky bucket.
- **Chat** — long-poll / WebSocket / push gateway.
- **Payments** — idempotency keys, double-entry ledgers, exactly-once.
- **Notifications** — fan-out + per-user prefs + delivery semantics.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Fan-out write** = cheap reads, expensive writes; **fan-out read** = opposite. Pick by `read:write` ratio.
- **Exactly-once payment** = idempotency key + DB-unique constraint, never trust delivery alone.
- **Geo-distributed** designs need consistency story — quorum read/write or Raft.
- **Hot keys** in URL shorteners — use base62 + counter sharding.
- **WebSocket scale** — sticky LB or central message bus.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For <case> the key constraint is <consistency | latency | scale>. I'd pick <fan-out / ledger / token-bucket> for that reason, partition by <key> for horizontal scale, and the bottleneck I'd deep-dive on is <component>."*
